final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is substantively more accurate than a clean-certification theory, but it does not satisfy the governing compliance predicate. The controlling evidence remains: the segment misses target, it is named in two utility pilot commitments, policy says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and legal review is still open with no final answer. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public risk-management principles may support a monitored-deployment concept in general, but they do not cure this specific unresolved internal policy requirement. This is the key distinction: a caveat can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat bounds residual risk after the compliance predicate is met; here, the caveat identifies the predicate that remains unmet. On the present admissible record, certification remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The policy makes the weakness material because the energy outage response segment is a named launch use case through two utility pilot commitments.
The record still lacks admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed before launch.
The record still lacks admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this named-use-case gap before launch.
The record still lacks admissible evidence that the evaluation gap was remediated before certification.
Legal review on disclosure remains open, so the disclosure predicate is unresolved rather than merely caveated.
